Results: The risk of GVHD-related death was lower among patients with higher intestinal diversity than among those with lower diversity.
The onset of aGVHD is associated with specific gut microbiota signatures. Non-aGVHD patients showed higher abundances of propionate-producing Bacteroidetes.
This aGVHD-predisposing ecosystem state was characterized by (i) reduced diversity, (ii) lower Blautia content, and (iii) an increase in Fusobacterium abundance.

The diversity was lower in the aGVHD group than the non-aGVHD group, and the Lachnospiraceae family of Clostridiales was decreased in the aGVHD group. The abundances of Blautia, Lachnoclostridium, Erysipelatoclostridium, and Eubacterium were lower in the aGVHD group than the non-aGVHD group.

The aGVHD group had a greater low microbial diversity than the non-aGVHD group. The bacterial community was depleted of Clostridia (e.g., the Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae families) and enriched for Gammaproteobacteria (e.g., the Enterobacteriaceae family) in the aGVHD group compared with the non-aGVHD group.
Dysbiosis of the intestines and acute GVHD occurred simultaneously, and Enterococcus species were abundant.
